opening.comment: The agent never gave their own name or the company name in the opening turn, so the greeting requirement was not met.

verification.quote: Agent: Yes. Thank you, Niamh, that matches your account.
verification.comment: The caller gave a full name and postcode, and the agent checked them against the account before discussing the order, which meets the requirement.

understanding.quote: Agent: sew the toaster arrived yesterday and doesn't turn on at all?
understanding.comment: The agent captured the issue (faulty toaster arrived yesterday), but the garbled wording and the mis-stated name make the recap unclear, and the caller's details were not confirmed properly.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Agent: I'll refund the full €22.00 to your card, you'll see it with in 5 working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: Items under EUR 25 do not need to go back, so the 'No' on return is correct, but the refund timeline is stated from the card side while policy says 5 working days from the warehouse receiving the return, which is not applicable here; the refund is for a faulty item so 5 working days is roughly right, though the agent should have stated the timeline accurately and offered a replacement option as well.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: I'll refund the full €22.00 to your card, you'll see it with in 5 working days.
process_compliance.comment: The agent did not ask for a photo of the faulty toaster before arranging the refund, which is a required step for damaged or faulty items.

communication.quote: Agent: I'm sorry it doesn't work out of the that's disappointing.
communication.comment: The agent apologised and acknowledged the disappointment, which is polite, though the sentence was garbled; the reply to 'Right, nothing' and the abrupt 'Right then' were curt.

closing.comment: The call ended without confirming next steps or asking if there was anything else, and the closing was abrupt and not polite.
